items.name: add-to-cart-button
items.title: Add To Cart Button
items.description: Add-to-cart button that sends a small paper price tag along an arc into the cart; the cart badge bumps like a stamp. Use on product cards and detail pages. Reduced motion skips the flight.

whenToUse: Product cards and quick-add rows in a shop
Any action that moves an item somewhere the user can see
watchOut: Point the flight at a cart icon that stays visible, or the motion has nowhere to land
Keep the server request independent of the animation so a slow network does not freeze it

items.name: addon-checklist
items.title: Add-on Checklist
items.description: A paper receipt of optional extras with dotted leaders between each item and its price, where every row is a checkbox and the subtotal rolls to its new value as you tick. Rows use role=checkbox with keyboard toggling, the subtotal is announced via aria-live, and the number jumps instantly under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Gift wrap, warranty and accessory upsells on a product or cart page
Booking extras such as parking, prints or insurance before checkout
watchOut: The total is display only; recalculate the price on the server from the selected ids
Required rows always count toward the total and cannot be unticked

items.name: animated-number
items.title: Animated Number
items.description: Mechanical odometer for prices and counts: each digit wheel turns in the direction the value moved, with Intl currency formatting and an optional small ink trend arrow. Screen readers get the formatted value.

whenToUse: Prices, totals and counters that change after a choice
Dashboard stats that update live
watchOut: Use tabular numbers so the width does not jump
Do not animate numbers that change many times a second

items.name: animation-editor
items.title: Animation Editor
items.description: Keyframe timeline from CardFlow: capture canvas snapshots, drag or type keyframe times, copy and delete them from a context menu or shortcuts, and play them back in a scroll-driven preview. The value is controlled, and helpers turn keyframes into framer-motion props or CSS @keyframes. Markers are focusable buttons with arrow-key time nudging, the context menu is keyboard reachable, and reduced motion removes the panel slide and fades.

whenToUse: Canvas or whiteboard apps where users capture layout states as keyframes and play them back
Scroll-driven storytelling where each keyframe is a full scene snapshot
watchOut: The default window-level Delete/Backspace shortcut deletes the selected keyframe; use shortcutScope="panel" or shortcutsEnabled={false} when the page has other editable content or canvas selection
Copying a keyframe renames its element ids (original behaviour), so the copy cross-fades rather than interpolates

items.name: announcement-strip
items.title: Announcement Strip
items.description: A paper strip notice bar for the top of the store with notched ends, manual previous and next for several messages, and a dismiss that collapses its height and is remembered under a storageKey. Messages sit in a labelled region with a polite live area, controls have ARIA labels, and the collapse is instant under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Site-wide notices such as free shipping thresholds, holiday returns or store hours
Rotating two or three short messages in one bar without auto-playing
watchOut: With a storageKey the strip renders after mount, so reserve no space for it or accept a small shift; change the key when the message changes
Keep each message to one line on mobile; long copy wraps and makes the bar tall

items.name: app-chip
items.title: App Chip
items.description: A project or app tag with a stable colour dot hashed from the app id and an optional paid mark; AppDot is exported for using the dot alone. The dot is aria-hidden, the paid mark has an aria-label, and nothing animates, so reduced motion needs no change.

whenToUse: Listing which apps or products a customer uses
Tagging records with a project whose colour stays the same everywhere
watchOut: appColor hashes the id into 8 colours, so two apps can share a colour
Long names truncate inside the chip; give the parent a width so it can shrink

items.name: assignment-sheet
items.title: Assignment Sheet
items.description: A "why this person" side sheet for a scheduled shift: the reasons, other candidates, a lock switch, and a find-replacement list with assign buttons. It is a labelled dialog with a role=switch lock, Escape to close and a polite live region for notices; reduced motion drops the slide and fades instantly.

whenToUse: Explaining why an automated scheduler or optimizer chose a person, with the alternatives it considered
Letting a manager lock, remove or reassign one assignment from its detail view
watchOut: onFindReplacement starts the load and replacement=null means loading; pass the result back through the replacement prop
Callbacks may throw to show an error notice; pass fixed={false} to render in place instead of as a fixed overlay

items.name: avatar-stack
items.title: Avatar Stack
items.description: Recent buyers social proof: initials on paper discs with an ink outline, a +N count and hover or focus tooltips. Use near add-to-cart to show real purchase activity.

whenToUse: Showing collaborators on a document, project or channel
Compact team rows in cards and table cells
watchOut: Each avatar is a tab stop so tooltips work by keyboard; keep max low in dense tables
Initials colors come from the name, so two people with the same name share a color

items.name: bill-split-rows
items.title: Bill Split Rows
items.description: An editable dish list for splitting a bill. Each row has dish, price and quantity fields, a delete button, Who ate it member toggles with an Everyone / Clear all switch, and a status line that shows the per-person share or why the dish isn't counted yet. Inputs are labelled, toggles use aria-pressed, bad numbers set aria-invalid, and the new-row pop-in is skipped under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Entering shared items (dishes, groceries, trip costs) and assigning who shares each
Any list of priced lines that are split evenly among chosen people
watchOut: Price and quantity are kept as raw strings and only whole numbers above 0 count, so parse them the same way downstream
Pass onRemove to route deletion through an undo flow; without it rows are deleted at once

items.name: browser-frame
items.title: Browser Frame
items.description: A desktop browser mockup with traffic lights, a tab title, a pill address bar with lock icon and an optional tone ring and Simulated badge. It renders as a figure labelled with the URL, the chrome is hidden from assistive tech, and nothing animates, so reduced motion needs no handling.

whenToUse: Presenting a web page or dashboard screenshot in docs, landing pages or slides
Framing a live embedded UI so readers know it represents a website
watchOut: The address bar is static text, not a real input
Set maxHeight for long content so it scrolls inside the frame instead of stretching the page

items.name: canvas-context-menu
items.title: Canvas Context Menu
items.description: A right-click menu for selected canvas objects with group or ungroup, layout, duplicate and delete, in CardFlow's frosted white glass with emoji icons and shortcut hints. It closes on an outside click or Escape, works as a keyboard menu (arrow keys, Home and End, focus returns on close), and only animates colour, which reduced motion turns off.

whenToUse: Right-click actions on selected objects in a whiteboard, canvas or design editor
Showing selection-aware actions such as grouping that only appear when they apply
watchOut: Keep the menu inside the viewport or container yourself: like the original, it opens exactly at x and y
Pass fixed={false} when it lives inside a relative container instead of the page

items.name: capsule-nav
items.title: Capsule Nav
items.description: A full-width blurred header that becomes a floating pill after you scroll past a threshold. It can hide while you scroll down, highlights the section in view and has a mobile menu panel. The menu traps focus, closes on Escape and the backdrop, and locks scroll. With reduced motion the morph and hide transitions switch instantly.

whenToUse: Marketing or portfolio pages with a few top-level links and one main call to action
Long single pages where the nav should show the current section
watchOut: Give target sections scroll-margin so the bar does not cover headings after an anchor jump
Inside a scroll container pass fixed={false} and scrollContainer, otherwise it listens to window

items.name: cardflow-loader
items.title: CardFlow Loader
items.description: A white loading screen with a circular progress ring, a percentage, a title and a rotating status line. It runs CardFlow's staged loading sequence by default or takes controlled progress. It fills its container by default, with an optional fullScreen prop. It exposes a progressbar with aria-valuenow and a polite live region; reduced motion turns off the ring transition.

whenToUse: A short boot screen before a canvas or app shell becomes interactive
Showing staged setup progress when you can report real percentages
watchOut: The default scripted sequence is about 0.9 s of fake progress; pass progress for real work
The status line changes every 10 s by default, so on short loads only the first message is seen

items.name: chapter-seekbar
items.title: Chapter Seekbar
items.description: A video seek bar split into chapter segments with 3px gaps. Segments sit at scaleY 0.6, grow to 1 on hover and to 1.7 under the pointer. It has a knob ringed in the accent colour, a hover chip with optional thumbnail, chapter title and time, and coloured markers with tooltips. It is a keyboard-operable slider (arrows 5 s, Shift 30 s, Home and End), and its transitions are disabled under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Long videos with named chapters or episodes
Showing bookmarks, clips or sponsor points on the timeline
watchOut: It is designed for a dark video overlay; the gap colours assume a dark backdrop
The hover chip stays 100px from each edge, so very narrow bars show it offset

items.name: character-glyph
items.title: Character Glyph
items.description: A seeded character avatar that shows one serif character from the name inside a style-pack shape (seal, circle, rounded square, hex or none), with a hashed colour inside the pack's saturation and lightness range; assignGlyphs gives earlier characters first pick so names in one cast do not collide. It is decorative (aria-hidden) unless a title is given, and it has no motion, so reduced motion needs no handling.

whenToUse: Character lists or casts for stories that have no character artwork
Avatars that must keep the same colour on every screen without images
watchOut: Use assignGlyphs for a whole cast in order; calling glyphSpec one by one can give two characters the same glyph
Minor tier characters drop their colour and use the muted text colour by design

items.name: checkin-streak
items.title: Check-in Streak
items.description: Daily check-in card with the last 7 days as circles (done filled, today outlined, missed dashed), a streak count, a reward toast, and a window event that tells quota displays to refresh. Days carry aria labels, the toast is a live region with a close button, and under reduced motion the spinner and toast motion are turned off.

whenToUse: Daily login or check-in rewards that add credits or quota
Showing a week of attendance next to a single claim action
watchOut: Pass today as a local YYYY-MM-DD so the 7-day window matches the server
Keep refreshEvent the same as the one your quota display listens to

items.name: checkout-steps
items.title: Checkout Steps
items.description: Compact checkout step row from the V窩 checkout: numbered pills that turn accent-filled with a check once done. Uses an ordered list with aria-current="step" and screen-reader text for completed steps; it is static, so nothing animates under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Showing where a buyer is in a short 2 to 4 step checkout above the step content
Multi-step forms where a full stepper with connectors would be too heavy
watchOut: Step names are used as React keys, so keep them unique
The theme follows prefers-color-scheme by default; pass theme="light" or "dark" if your site uses a class toggle

items.name: choice-cards
items.title: Choice Cards
items.description: World-choice dialogue from voxel-world. Equal-height portrait cards deal in one by one, each with a path colour, an art slot, a name banner, a brief, green gains and red costs. Below them a dialogue box with a name plate shows what the selected card means. Supports roving focus, arrow keys and WASD, digit keys, Enter or Space to pick, Escape or gamepad B to close, and gamepad d-pad and A. Disabled cards stay readable with their reason, and reduced motion turns off the deal-in, glow and float.

whenToUse: Story branch points with two to three paths, each with clear gains and costs
Choices that need art and a one-line explanation of what picking each means
watchOut: Picking happens on click, Enter or a digit key, with no extra confirm step, so use it only where the pick is the action
Keep gains and costs to one short visible fact per line; long reasons wrap inside the card

items.name: cjk-heading
items.title: CJK Heading
items.description: Typeset Traditional Chinese and Japanese campaign headlines: punctuation compression, CJK and Latin spacing, optional vertical writing and a vermilion seal highlight for one key word. No motion.

whenToUse: Chinese or Japanese headlines on landing pages
Editorial layouts that want vertical writing
watchOut: Vertical writing needs a fixed height and short lines
Check punctuation placement in every target font

items.name: classic-card
items.title: Classic Card
items.description: The original SunUI card with five variants (outlined, filled, elevated, glass, gradient), six colour themes, light and dark modes, four sizes, an optional hover glow, and skeleton, shimmer and overlay loading states. Clickable cards act as buttons you can focus and trigger with Enter or Space, loading sets aria-busy and announces itself, and reduced motion turns off the entrance, hover and tap animations.

whenToUse: Product, article or feature tiles that need a themed, decorative surface such as glass, gradient or glow
Content blocks that load asynchronously and need a skeleton, shimmer or spinner state in place
watchOut: Glass and gradient variants are semi-transparent: put them over a coloured or busy background or they look washed out
Add the group class to the Card if you want the CardImage hover zoom and overlay to fire

items.name: classic-countdown-banner
items.title: Classic Countdown Banner
items.description: The original SunUI promo countdown: a discount headline, struck-through price, four flipping time boxes, drifting particles and a glowing CTA, in 5 themes, 3 layouts (default, spacious, modern), 3 variants (card, banner, floating), light and dark modes, and zh/en labels. The timer exposes role="timer" with a summary down to the minute, and decorative parts are aria-hidden. With reduced motion, the entrance, digit flips, particles and pulse loops all switch instantly or stay still.

whenToUse: Hero or mid-page promo for a time-limited sale with a clear discount and price drop
A floating sale card that stays visible while a product page scrolls
watchOut: The modern card layout is tall and visually loud, so use one per page
Countdown labels are short (Hrs, Min); override them with labels for other locales

items.name: classic-file-upload
items.title: Classic File Upload
items.description: SunUI's original animated drop zone: violet, cyan, orange or custom themes, a bobbing upload icon, a drag-over prompt, image thumbnails or compact rows, a shimmering progress overlay, and size and type checks with an error toast. It works as a keyboard-operable button, reports progress through a progressbar with a polite live region, and stops all looping motion when reduced motion is on.

whenToUse: Attaching images, PDFs or documents to a form or project with a visible preview
A single focused upload area where drag and drop and click to browse should both work
watchOut: By default progress is simulated (0 to 100 in about 330 ms) before onFileUpload resolves; pass simulateProgress={false} and call onProgress to show real progress
PDF thumbnails need a renderPdfPreview function (for example built on pdfjs-dist); without one PDFs show a file icon

items.name: classic-filter-grid
items.title: Classic Filter Grid
items.description: SunUI's original skill and icon wall: hexagon, square or circle tiles in light, dark, blue, green or purple themes, with category pills, pagination or infinite scroll, pulsing loading skeletons and a springy hover tilt. Category pills use aria-pressed, pagination is a labelled nav with aria-current, clickable tiles are keyboard buttons, and reduced motion removes the spring entrance, hover tilt and skeleton pulse.

whenToUse: Portfolio skill or tech-stack walls grouped by category
Icon catalogs or integration lists that need lightweight filtering and paging
watchOut: The blue, green, purple and dark themes use light text and assume a dark page background
Only GridItem children are rendered; anything else passed as a child is ignored

items.name: classic-floating-button
items.title: Classic Floating Button
items.description: The original SunUI floating action button. Its gradient links fan out as petals, stack vertically or spread as a grid from any corner, and it supports controlled or uncontrolled state, a mode without the toggle button, and dragging with position memory. The toggle has an accessible name and aria-expanded, links are labelled, and springs and pops switch instantly under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Social or share links on a portfolio or blog that should stay one tap away
A compact cluster of quick actions in a page corner that the user may want to move aside
watchOut: The petal radius grows 56px per layer, so many links need room around the corner
Links open in a new tab; give buttons a title or type so each one has an accessible name

items.name: classic-gradient-background
items.title: Classic Gradient Background
items.description: An animated radial gradient with two glow layers that breathe on offset timings and a fine grid overlay, from the original SunUI package. By default it fills its relative parent; fullScreen pins it behind the whole viewport. It is aria-hidden and ignores the pointer, and reduced motion freezes the glows on their first frame.

whenToUse: Hero sections and landing headers that need a dark, glowing backdrop
Feature panels or tiles that should feel lit from behind
watchOut: Colours must be 6-digit hex, because the glow and grid layers add a two-digit alpha suffix
The parent needs relative (and isolate or overflow-hidden) or the background escapes it

items.name: classic-side-panel
items.title: Classic Side Panel
items.description: The original SunUI slide-in side panel: left or right, six color themes in light and dark, an edge toggle button, Escape and outside-click closing, an optional overlay, a built-in date range selector, and a provider so several panels can share state. It is a labelled dialog with focus moved in and restored, and slides switch instantly under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Dashboard filters or settings that slide in from the edge without leaving the page
Several independent drawers (left and right) that should not show competing toggle buttons
watchOut: The edge toggle button is hidden below the sm breakpoint, so give small screens an in-page trigger
Wrap multiple panels in SidePanelProvider, otherwise hideButtonsWhenAnyOpen has no effect

items.name: classic-social-button
items.title: Classic Social Button
items.description: Round gradient social link buttons with tooltips (always, on hover or hidden; top, right, bottom or left), a main-button mode, and a SocialButtonGroup that fans the links out in petal, vertical or grid layouts. Each link takes its accessible name from the title, tooltips also show on keyboard focus, the main button reports aria-expanded, and reduced motion turns the scale and spring animations into instant changes.

whenToUse: Profile cards and footers that link to social accounts
A compact expandable cluster of contact links in a page corner
watchOut: Each SocialButton link is absolutely positioned, so wrap it in a relative h-10 w-10 box when you place it in normal layout
Expanded petal and vertical groups reach about 150 to 230px from the corner, so leave room or the parent will clip them

items.name: combine-dialog
items.title: Combine Dialog
items.description: Dark dialog that stitches a post's images into one postable image or a PDF. It has a live preview, layout chips (restore panorama, N columns, single row), a locked chip for paid layouts, a gap option and thumbnails you can leave out. It is a labelled modal dialog that closes on Escape, and its entrance animation is turned off under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Stitching several images of a carousel into one image to repost
Restoring a panorama that was split across several slides
watchOut: Give every image its real width and height or the layout math cannot work
Throw from onSaveImages to keep the dialog open so people can switch layout or save a PDF instead

items.name: compare-slider
items.title: Compare Slider
items.description: Before and after comparison with a draggable divider over a transparent native range input, so click to jump, arrow keys and screen readers all work. An optional demo sweep runs once when the slider first scrolls into view and stops the moment the user touches it. It is skipped under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Showing an uploaded original next to a generated or edited result
Retouch, upscale or restyle previews where the difference is spatial
watchOut: The frame follows the result's ratio; a before image with another ratio is letterboxed, not cropped
Keep the demo sweep to one slider per screen

items.name: confirm-button
items.title: Confirm Button
items.description: Press-twice confirm with no modal. The first press arms the button, swaps its label to the outcome and shows a short notice. A second press within 2.5 s runs the action, and the result appears in a polite status line. It uses usermeld's shadcn button variants and sizes, Escape disarms it, and the spinner respects reduced motion.

whenToUse: Irreversible row actions in admin tables where a dialog would be too heavy
Actions that lose progress, such as quick load, where one misclick should not commit
watchOut: Name confirmLabel after the outcome ("Remove signup"), not "Confirm"
The notice line reserves a little height under the button; account for it in dense tables

items.name: content-gate
items.title: Content Gate
items.description: Inline locked-course card with a glow, lock badge, gradient title and a sign-in button that shows a spinner and disables itself after one press, with different copy for signed-out and no-access visitors. Follows light and dark themes, announces the sign-in state politely to screen readers, and the spinner only spins when reduced motion is off.

whenToUse: A paid course or members page reached by someone signed out
A signed-in visitor whose account has no purchase for this content
watchOut: Pass signInHref or onSignIn; after a press the button stays disabled until the page navigates
Give the parent enough height; the card centers itself with vertical padding

items.name: copy-code-button
items.title: Copy Code Button
items.description: Printed promo code slip with a dashed outline; copying presses a small vermilion COPIED stamp and announces the result. Falls back when the clipboard API is unavailable.

whenToUse: Coupon and promo codes in checkout or emails
Any short string the user needs to paste elsewhere
watchOut: Clipboard access needs a secure context (https or localhost)
Keep the code visible as text so it can still be copied by hand

items.name: countdown-banner
items.title: Countdown Banner
items.description: Paper sale banner with discount, prices and a printed flip-card countdown to a real end date; shows an ended stamp when time is up. Supports English and Chinese copy.

whenToUse: Time limited sales with a real end time
Launch day announcements
watchOut: Only show a countdown that reflects a real deadline
Render the end time on the server so every visitor sees the same clock

items.name: coupon-wallet
items.title: Coupon Wallet
items.description: A stack of owned coupons that fans out on hover, keyboard focus or a first tap, so shoppers can compare and pick one to apply, which stamps it Applied. It is a radiogroup with roving focus (arrow keys, Home, End, Escape to collapse), ineligible coupons explain why in their label, and the fan snaps into place without motion under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Choosing which of several owned coupons to apply at checkout or in the cart
A compact coupon picker where a full list would push the order summary off screen
watchOut: The fan is about 1.5 card widths wide, so give it a column of at least 22rem or keep it to four coupons
Recalculate the discount on the server; the selection only tells you which coupon the shopper picked

items.name: dialogue-box
items.title: Dialogue Box
items.description: A visual-novel narration overlay. Narration floats without a box; spoken lines get a seal-dot name plate. Text types out at a jitter-free reserved height, with a kinsoku-safe next-line cue (caret, or a feather in the moon theme) that turns into an autoplay countdown ring. It also has choices with 【requirement】 tags, a log, autoplay and fast-forward controls, and number-key, Enter/Space, A, L and held-Ctrl shortcuts. Screen readers hear each whole line once; with reduced motion the cue and choice animations stop and the ring becomes a static dot.

whenToUse: Ink, Yarn or custom-script visual novels and narrative RPG scenes over a background
Branching choices that show stat requirements, locked options and already-picked marks
watchOut: Place it inside a relative container with a real height; all layers are absolutely positioned
Pass a stable lineId per line so read state, fast-forward and the typewriter reset correctly

items.name: director-review
items.title: Director Review
items.description: A dark AI edit-suggestion review where each card shows confidence and risk. Safe suggestions are preselected, the batch actions are accept-safe or reject-all, and edits that change video length must be accepted one at a time (computePlanTotals is exported). Cards are labelled groups, the plan summary is a polite live region, and transitions are disabled under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Reviewing AI-proposed edits to a recording before they are applied to a timeline
Any batch of suggestions where safe ones can be preselected but destructive ones need explicit consent
watchOut: Decisions are uncontrolled unless you pass decisions with onDecisionsChange
appliedKinds decides which cards say "preview only" and which count toward the length change; pass a stable array

items.name: drawing-toolbar
items.title: Drawing Toolbar
items.description: CardFlow's glass drawing rail (pen, line, rectangle, circle, arrow) with the P and 1 to 4 shortcuts, plus a DrawingSurface that draws freehand strokes and shapes with a live preview, and the colour and width DrawingPanel. Tools use aria-pressed and aria-keyshortcuts, Escape leaves drawing mode, and reduced motion removes the slide and hover scale.

whenToUse: Adding a sketch or annotation mode to a canvas, whiteboard or screenshot markup tool
Letting people circle and point at things with quick shape tools
watchOut: The global shortcuts are on while the toolbar is open; set shortcuts={false} if other keyboard handlers clash
Strokes use the surface's own pixel coordinates; pan and zoom are not handled, so transform the points yourself on a zoomable canvas

items.name: empty-state
items.title: Empty State
items.description: Dashed empty-state card with a 1.5-stroke icon, title, description and a Load example plus outline button pair (or a custom action), centered or start-aligned. Buttons are real buttons or links with visible focus rings; it is static, so nothing animates under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Lists or tables that have no data yet and need a clear next step
First-run screens where loading an example teaches the product faster than an empty form
watchOut: Passing action replaces the built-in Load example and secondary buttons
Keep the description to one or two short sentences so the card stays scannable

items.name: error-state
items.title: Error State
items.description: Error panel with a warning icon, friendly title and message, and an optional Retry button. Uses role="alert" so screen readers announce it; it is static, so nothing animates under reduced motion.

whenToUse: A list or panel whose data request failed and can be retried
Replacing a section in place when it cannot load, without breaking the rest of the page
watchOut: Never pass raw exceptions as the message; map them to friendly text first
Omit onRetry when retrying cannot help, so users are not sent in a loop

items.name: expanding-search
items.title: Expanding Search
items.description: Store search field that expands into a paper slip of product suggestions with thumbnails, prices and keyboard navigation (combobox pattern, / shortcut).

whenToUse: Compact navbars where a full search field does not fit
Sites where search is secondary but should stay one click away
watchOut: Leave room in the layout for the expanded width so neighbouring items do not jump
Built-in filtering is a simple substring match; set filterSuggestions to false for server results

items.name: favorite-button
items.title: Favorite Button
items.description: Wishlist heart in ink that fills vermilion with a stamp-like press when saved. aria-pressed toggle with optional count.

whenToUse: Wishlists, likes and saves on product or content cards
Lightweight toggles that deserve a little delight
watchOut: Update the count optimistically and roll back on error
Give it an accessible name that includes the item

items.name: flip-profile-card
items.title: Flip Profile Card
items.description: A gradient profile card that tilts in 3D toward the mouse and flips on click to a details back, with seven light effect modes and seven colour themes, plus matching theme and light effect pickers. A focusable flip button with aria-pressed, inert on the hidden face, and radiogroup pickers with arrow keys; pointer effects run only on fine pointers, and reduced motion disables tilt and makes the flip instant.

whenToUse: A personal or team member business card that people can flip for bio, skills and links
A profile card editor where users preview colour themes and lighting live
watchOut: Keep back-face content short: the card is a fixed 384px tall and the back does not scroll
The glassmorphism theme is white on translucent glass, so it needs a coloured or busy backdrop to read

items.name: floating-toolbar
items.title: Floating Toolbar
items.description: CardFlow's vertical glass tool rail with dark tooltips, a selected state and a 300ms slide in and out, set up as the AI actions toolbar: Generate calls an async onAction and shows a spinner while it runs. Tools use aria-pressed and aria-keyshortcuts, Escape goes back when onClose is set, and reduced motion removes the slide and scale transitions.

whenToUse: A side tool rail in a canvas or editor
Running an async AI action from a toolbar button with built-in pending feedback
watchOut: Handle errors inside onAction: the toolbar only clears its pending state and selection
To swap two toolbars pass open to each, and give the canvas overflow hidden so the hidden one slides off-screen

items.name: gate-modal
items.title: Gate Modal
items.description: Designed dark access modal (165 degree gradient panel, gradient top line, two blurred glows, gradient title, note box and gradient sign-in button) for locked lessons, with signed-out and no-access copy. It traps focus, closes on Escape and the backdrop, locks scroll and returns focus to the trigger; it uses no motion, so it is safe under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Someone clicks a locked lesson or episode inside a course page
Asking for sign-in at the moment of intent instead of blocking the whole page
watchOut: The modal is dark only by design; use content-gate on themed pages
Pass fixed={false} only when a relative parent should hold the modal (no portal, no scroll lock)

items.name: hold-to-redeem
items.title: Hold to Redeem
items.description: Press-and-hold confirm drawn as the voxel-world HUD ring around a gold keycap. It fills while held, rewinds when released, and turns red and rewinds if the confirm fails. An optional warning zone flashes the ring, shows a "!" and asks you to release. Works with pointer and keyboard (Space, Enter or the keycap letter) and has a polite live region. With reduced motion the rewind is instant and there is no pulse or flashing.

whenToUse: Spending in-game currency or another irreversible redeem where a held press shows intent
Game-styled confirms where a last-chance warning near the end of the hold helps
watchOut: Holding is harder for some motor abilities; keep holdMs short (default 700 ms, as in the source) and keep keyboard support
The look is a dark pixel panel built for game UI, not neutral app chrome

items.name: honest-countdown
items.title: Honest Countdown
items.description: Countdown to a real start time (a live stream or event) in mono day/hour/min/sec cells. It shows only the date before hydration, switches to a pulsing "Live now" and then an ended line, and never invents a deadline. Screen readers get one static sentence (status role when live) instead of a ticking number, and the pulse stops under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Hero of an event or live-stream landing page
Session lists that should show upcoming, live and ended states from the same data
watchOut: Built for dark surfaces (white-alpha cells, gold accent); put it on a dark hero
Pass the real start and end times from your backend; it counts to the start, not to a sign-up cutoff

items.name: hover-card
items.title: Hover Card
items.description: A product quick-view card that opens after a short hover delay and stays open while the pointer moves into it, with price, discount and an add to cart button on paper. Keyboard focus opens it, Escape closes it and returns focus, touch opens it on first tap, it flips above the trigger near the viewport edge, and reduced motion removes the slide.

whenToUse: Product names inside carts, bundles or editorial text where a quick preview saves a page visit
Recommendation lists where shoppers compare price before opening the product page
watchOut: It is positioned inside its parent, so an overflow hidden ancestor will clip the card
Keep essential information on the product page too; the card is a shortcut, not the only place

items.name: infinite-avatar-grid
items.title: Infinite Avatar Grid
items.description: A pannable, zoomable infinite canvas of round avatars that only renders the visible cells. Avatars bubble in with a spring curve, and selecting one opens a gradient profile card. Keyboard accessible (arrow keys pan, plus and minus zoom, Enter opens, Escape closes the dialog); reduced motion skips the bubble and card transitions.

whenToUse: Browsing a large or unbounded directory of people as a spatial wall rather than a list
Playful discovery screens where users drag around and tap faces to see a profile card
watchOut: The wheel listener calls preventDefault, so page scroll stops while the pointer is over the grid; give it a bounded height
getUser must be deterministic per coordinate and cheap, since it runs for every visible cell on each pan or zoom settle

items.name: issue-card
items.title: Scan Issue Card
items.description: One code scan issue with severity, category and AI badges, a fix suggestion that expands to show before and after with steps, and a code viewer that highlights the problem lines. Toggles use aria-expanded and the dialog closes on Escape; reduced motion removes the press and hover transitions.

whenToUse: Static analysis or security scan result lists
Code review tools showing an issue with a suggested fix
watchOut: Ignore asks for confirmation through window.confirm unless you pass confirmIgnore
The Before and After boxes use light red and green backgrounds even in dark mode, as in the original

items.name: job-panel
items.title: Job Panel
items.description: The side panel of a generation progress page: a status heading, ETA or duration, a progress bar with five named steps, queue position, error or hold notes, and cancel, cancel and edit, retry or remove actions. It has a polite live heading, a progressbar role, aria-current on the current step and an alert region for failed actions; under reduced motion the spinner and note animation stop.

whenToUse: A job detail page that shows where a generation is and lets the user cancel or retry
Long-running AI tasks with distinct queue, load, generate and check stages
watchOut: Return a rejecting Promise from an action to show its inline error
Pass the prompt or rewrite result as children so it sits between steps and actions

items.name: job-row
items.title: Job Row
items.description: A compact console row for a job in flight: title, source type, a thin progress bar with a stage label and percent, or a failure line, linking to the job's detail page; it ships with JobStatusDot, a dot and text status marker. It has a progressbar role and a visible focus outline; under reduced motion the bar transition and running dot pulse stop.

whenToUse: A dashboard list of jobs in progress that link to their detail pages
A quiet status row where a full card would be too heavy
watchOut: Pass the progress as 0 to 100 and a short stage label
Set failed to replace the bar with the retry hint instead of showing 0%

items.name: job-tile
items.title: Job Tile
items.description: A grid tile for one AI generation job: a shimmer over the blurred reference image, a status line, a non-linear progress bar and ETA, which turns into a dashed tile with a reason once the job fails, is canceled or is held. It has a progressbar role, a polite live status, aria-busy and labelled cancel and remove buttons; under reduced motion the shimmer, spinner and preview transition stop.

whenToUse: An image or video generation grid where pending jobs sit beside finished results
Showing queue, model loading and sampling progress right where the result will appear
watchOut: Replace the tile with the result image when the job is done
Keep the non-linear percent mapping so sampling covers most of the bar

items.name: jobs-tray
items.title: Jobs Tray
items.description: A bottom-right stack of background job rows with a pulsing dot, a percent or state label, cancel on running jobs and dismiss on failed ones, plus a useBackgroundJobs hook. The list is a polite live region and the pulse is switched off under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Saving, encoding or exporting continues after the user is allowed back into the editor
Surfacing background failures that need the user's attention
watchOut: Successful jobs are removed after 8 s and quick ones are never shown, so do not rely on the tray as a log
Keep failed rows until dismissed; they are the reason the tray exists

items.name: karaoke-caption
items.title: Karaoke Caption
items.description: A dark rounded caption pill that lights up the token being spoken: one Chinese character or one Latin word at a time. Spoken tokens turn white, the active one gold, and upcoming ones dim. The font size adjusts to the sentence length. Screen readers hear each sentence once through a polite live region, and reduced motion removes the colour transitions.

whenToUse: Narrated videos, podcasts or slide decks where viewers follow the voice word by word
Two-speaker shows where each speaker gets their own accent colour
watchOut: Token timing is spread evenly across the sentence, so it only roughly matches the speech
In a gap between sentences it keeps showing the nearest one; set holdNearest={false} to hide it instead

items.name: link-preview-card
items.title: Link Preview Card
items.description: CardFlow link card: shows the Open Graph site name, title, description and image, with a loading overlay, empty and invalid-URL states, and an optional iframe web view that falls back to the card when the site blocks framing. Opens on double-click, right-click or Enter/Space; the hover toolbar also appears on keyboard focus, icon buttons have aria-labels, and transitions turn off under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Turning a pasted URL into a rich card on a board, canvas or feed
Showing bookmarks where the metadata comes from your own Open Graph endpoint
watchOut: fetchPreview must call your own server route; browsers cannot read another site's HTML because of CORS
The iframe view only works for sites that allow framing; turn it off with allowEmbed={false} for untrusted URLs

items.name: live-bento
items.title: Live Bento
items.description: A feature bento grid whose tiles blur in on scroll and lift on hover, with a useTicker hook so each tile's own small visual replays only while visible; the lb-* keyframes are injected for those visuals. Visuals are aria-hidden so the tile title and body carry the meaning, and with reduced motion tiles appear instantly and tickers stop on the first frame.

whenToUse: A 'more features' section where each feature needs a tiny living illustration
Showing secondary capabilities below a hero without heavy media
watchOut: Each tile visual runs its own observer and timer, so keep one grid to around 6 to 9 tiles
Visuals that use lb-* classes must sit inside <LiveBento>, which injects the keyframes

items.name: loading-state
items.title: Loading State
items.description: Skeleton loading placeholder made of pulsing rows. Exposes role="status" with an accessible label, and the pulse stops under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Lists and tables while their first page of data is loading
Keeping layout stable while a section refetches
watchOut: Match the row count to the real content so the layout does not jump
Give label a specific name like Loading past bills instead of the generic default

items.name: logo-menu
items.title: Logo Menu
items.description: CardFlow's logo button that grows a pill of icon nav links on hover or focus, downward or to the right, and collapses 150ms after the pointer leaves. The logo button reports aria-expanded, links sit in a labelled nav, Escape collapses it, and reduced motion removes the expand transition.

whenToUse: A compact corner entry point to a few pages in a canvas app
Hiding secondary navigation behind the brand mark
watchOut: Every item is icon only, so give each a clear label (used for aria-label and title)
It positions itself absolute at the top left, so place it inside a relative container

items.name: low-stock-indicator
items.title: Low Stock Indicator
items.description: Honest printed stock tag: one slip per unit when stock is small, otherwise a thin ink line; vermilion only at the critical level and a stamp when sold out. Never counts down on its own.

whenToUse: Product pages where stock is genuinely limited
Ticket and seat selection
watchOut: Only show real inventory numbers, fake scarcity erodes trust
Hide it entirely when stock is comfortable

items.name: markdown-card
items.title: Markdown Card
items.description: Notion-style markdown card from CardFlow: selecting it switches to a monospace textarea after 100 ms, and Escape or blurring outside the card returns to the rendered preview with Notion-like heading, list, code, quote and link styles. The preview can be focused and opens the editor with Enter, Escape hands focus back to the preview, the textarea has a label, and transitions turn off under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Sticky-note or document cards on a canvas that edit in place
Short notes where users write markdown and read the formatted result
watchOut: The editor is a plain textarea with no toolbar or syntax highlighting
Escape is listened for on window while editing, so it can clash with other Escape handlers such as dialogs

items.name: media-picker
items.title: Media Picker
items.description: Dark dialog for choosing which images and videos of a post to download: everything starts selected, with check and play badges, a remembered include-text option, and resolveMediaPick to skip the dialog when there is a single item. Tiles are toggle buttons with aria-pressed, Escape and backdrop click close it, and there is no motion to reduce.

whenToUse: Saving only some media from a post, carousel or gallery
Letting people add the post text to a media download
watchOut: Call resolveMediaPick first so a post with one item downloads directly without opening the dialog
Pass persistKey={null} if the include-text choice should not be stored in localStorage

items.name: notice-queue
items.title: Notice Queue
items.description: A first-in, first-out story notice lane that shows one notice at a time: compact found-item cards with a glyph, kicker, shimmering title and +N queue count, or one-line bond notices with an optional seal. Each lives 4.2s, ink-bleeds in and retracts over the last 280ms, pauses on hover or focus, closes with Esc and can open a detail view. It is a polite live region; with reduced motion there is no exit animation, bleed or shimmer.

whenToUse: Announcing clues, items, stat growth or relationship changes in a narrative game without interrupting reading
A single top-right feedback lane fed by several producers that must never cover each other
watchOut: Hold the queue (holding prop) while a detail view opened from a notice is showing, so it is not dismissed underneath
Keep titles short; long titles are cut off with an ellipsis at 17rem

items.name: numbered-steps
items.title: Numbered Steps
items.description: Numbered instruction list from the V窩 checkout, with soft info-tinted number badges and rich content (bold, links) per step. Keeps ordered-list semantics with sr-only step prefixes and aria-hidden visual numbers; it is static, so nothing animates under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Short how-to instructions next to a payment or setup action
Explaining what happens after a button press in two to four steps
watchOut: Keep each step to one or two sentences; long steps belong in docs
The theme follows prefers-color-scheme by default; pass theme="light" or "dark" if your site uses a class toggle

items.name: order-history
items.title: Order History
items.description: A receipt-style list of past orders with small status stamps, expandable line items with dotted leaders and totals, an actions slot for buy again or track, and an empty state. Each row is a disclosure button with aria-expanded and aria-controls, and the expand and collapse are instant under reduced motion.

whenToUse: The orders tab of a customer account page
A recent orders panel on an account dashboard with buy again shortcuts
watchOut: Totals are computed from line items, shipping and discount on the client; pass server-confirmed values so they match the real charge
For a single order's shipping timeline use order-tracker instead

items.name: otp-input
items.title: OTP Input
items.description: One-time code entry styled like boxes on a printed form: auto-advance, paste to fill, keyboard navigation, a short error shake and a VERIFIED stamp.

whenToUse: Sign in and two step verification codes
Short numeric codes from SMS or email
watchOut: Keep autocomplete one-time-code so phones can autofill
Do not auto-submit before the last digit is entered

items.name: pagination
items.title: Pagination
items.description: Page navigation with a fixed width ellipsis range (first, last, current and siblings), previous and next controls, aria-current="page" and an optional compact '3 / 12' mode; pass getHref to render crawlable links or onPageChange for buttons. A small underline slides to the current page with a snappy spring, and jumps instantly under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Product listing, search result and order history pages with a known page count
SEO sensitive catalogues where every page needs a real link
watchOut: Use getHref for pages that should be indexed; buttons alone are invisible to crawlers
For endless feeds without a total count, prefer a load more button

items.name: pause-menu
items.title: Pause Menu
items.description: An in-game system menu: a faded ink band with brush-sweep hover items, the current objective, a save-error banner, and an exit confirmation that names the last autosave and offers a save-first option. The dialog is modal, takes focus and closes with Esc; with reduced motion the entrance animations are dropped.

whenToUse: Pause or system menu in a narrative or exploration game
Any destructive exit that should say exactly what progress will be lost and where the player can resume
watchOut: Pass lastAutosave as a readable chapter · scene · time line, never an internal id
Close the pause menu when opening a save panel so the two Esc handlers do not both fire

items.name: payment-status-banner
items.title: Payment Status Banner
items.description: Frosted full-width banner shown when a buyer returns from checkout: pending polls every 3 s up to 8 times and turns into success once access is unlocked, success stays and links to the course, failed and error close themselves after 8 s. Uses role="status" for pending and success and role="alert" for failures, has a labelled close button, and the spinner stops under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Landing page after a hosted payment redirect (?checkout=success|pending|failed|error)
Payments where a webhook unlocks access some seconds after the redirect
watchOut: onRefresh must actually refetch and update the unlocked prop, otherwise pending never turns into success
Colours are tuned for dark pages; set fixed={false} when placing it inside a layout

items.name: permission-center
items.title: Permission Center
items.description: Dark macOS permission panel from KapZoom listing screen recording, microphone and camera with a status dot, what breaks without each grant, and Request or Open System Settings actions. Status is text as well as color, all actions are real buttons with focus rings, and it has no motion to reduce.

whenToUse: A settings or onboarding view that explains which OS permissions a recorder needs
Letting users recover from a denied permission without leaving the flow blind
watchOut: Screen recording cannot be requested in-app on macOS; only offer Open System Settings for it
Mark only truly required grants as required so optional ones read as degradations

items.name: person-chip
items.title: Person Chip
items.description: A name chip with a stable identity-colour dot keyed to the person's id, with states for emphasized (self), selected, highlighted (changed), muted and locked; EmployeeChip is the same component keyed by employeeId. Clickable chips render as buttons with aria-pressed, the lock icon is labelled, and the hover transition is removed under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Staff or member rows on schedules and rosters where each person keeps the same colour on every screen
Selecting one person to open details in a side panel
watchOut: personColor cycles 8 colours by id modulo, so different ids can share a colour; never use colour as the only identifier
Pass onClick to get a button with aria-pressed; without it the chip is a plain span

items.name: phone-frame
items.title: Phone Frame
items.description: A phone mockup with a dynamic island, status bar (time, signal, wifi, battery), an optional browser URL bar and a home indicator, with a compact layout below 240px width. It renders as a labelled figure with the decorative chrome hidden from assistive tech, and nothing animates, so reduced motion needs no handling.

whenToUse: Showing a mobile screen or mobile web page next to an article or pitch
Previewing how a flow such as a cart or checkout looks on a phone
watchOut: The width is fixed in pixels and shrinks to 100% in narrow containers; set height so long content scrolls inside the screen
It is a mockup; pass badge (for example Simulated) when the content is drawn, not recorded

items.name: preflight-checklist
items.title: Recording Preflight Checks
items.description: KapZoom-style live check bar beside the Start Recording button: warnings and blockers stay visible, passing items fold into an 'N look fine' popover, and buildPreflightChecks turns permissions, mic health, disk space and privacy scope into ordered checks. The list is a polite live region, the popover toggle reports aria-expanded, and the chevron and spinner stop under reduced motion.

whenToUse: The bottom bar of the last screen before a screen, camera or audio recording starts
Surfacing missing permissions, low disk space and privacy risks without a blocking dialog
watchOut: Only blockers should disable Start; keep disk and mic issues at warning level
Rebuild checks from fresh input on every change instead of patching the array

items.name: preview-paywall
items.title: Preview Paywall
items.description: Blurred gradient overlay with a lock, preview-count message and gold gradient call to action, placed over a player when a free preview of slides or episodes runs out. It is a labelled region whose call to action is a real link or button, and it has no animation, so reduced motion needs no change.

whenToUse: Capping a free preview of slides or episodes and sending people to buy
Covering a player or reader once the visitor reaches the last free item
watchOut: The parent must be position: relative; the overlay fills it absolutely
Controls you want usable under the overlay need a z-index above 40

items.name: print-preview
items.title: A4 Print Preview
items.description: Stacks content on real-size A4 sheets and puts each page break at the nearest block boundary, so headings and list items are not cut. Each page is a labelled group, duplicate page copies are hidden from assistive tech, and there is no animation, so it is reduced-motion safe.

whenToUse: Resume or document builders with a live A4 preview
Showing how a report will paginate before PDF export
watchOut: Content is rendered once per page, so avoid ids or heavy widgets inside it
Blocks taller than one page are still cut at the page height

items.name: quantity-stepper
items.title: Quantity Stepper
items.description: Receipt-style quantity stepper with tabular count, long-press repeat, typed input, min and max limits and a remove action at the minimum.

whenToUse: Cart and checkout line items
Any bounded numeric input changed in small steps
watchOut: The plus and minus buttons are removed from the tab order; keyboard users adjust via the field itself
Typed values snap to the nearest step, so tell users when step is larger than 1

items.name: quota-meter
items.title: Quota Meter
items.description: Remaining quota as a percent plus about how many images are left, in three forms: sidebar ring, mobile sheet bar, and plans-page card. When today's check-in is unclaimed, the second line becomes a check-in nudge. The included hook refetches on window focus, on route or job-count change, and on the rewards event. It uses progressbar roles, an aria-labelled link and a focus-reachable tooltip when the sidebar is collapsed, and drops transitions under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Showing remaining generation quota in an app sidebar or account sheet
A plans page summary with a nudge toward a daily reward
watchOut: Show images and percent, never raw credits, to match the source wording
Pass a refreshKey that changes when a job finishes so the meter updates

items.name: recording-hud
items.title: Recording HUD
items.description: A draggable dark glass pill for screen recording with a blinking record dot, mono timer, pause/resume, an optional pen with draw swatches and Clear, and stop. Buttons have aria labels and pressed states, Esc closes the pen, and the blink and palette transitions stop under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Controls that float over content being screen recorded
A compact timer plus pause and stop that the user can drag out of the way
watchOut: Only enable the pen when recording a whole screen; it means nothing for a single window
Push seconds from the recorder; the HUD's own 1 s count is only a fallback

items.name: recording-sidebar
items.title: Recording Sidebar
items.description: KapZoom recording options sidebar with microphone and system audio switches, a mic level meter fed by a subscription, camera toggle, countdown segmented control and a collapsed Advanced section for cursor, performance and quality. Toggles are role=switch, segments use aria-pressed, mic status is announced in a polite live region, and the meter and switch transitions stop under reduced motion.

whenToUse: The settings column next to a recording source picker
Letting users test their mic level before a capture starts
watchOut: Pass the mic level as a subscription, not React state, so the meter does not re-render the sidebar
Arm the mic probe on user action so the OS permission prompt does not appear unprompted

items.name: redeem-key-input
items.title: License and Redeem Panel
items.description: Dark license panel with one input that tells a 12-character supporter code from a Lemon Squeezy UUID key and sends each the right way. It shows the free, trial, basic, pro and supporter tiers, explains grace, expired and invalid states, and offers activate, deactivate and revalidate. Provider errors become messages that say what to do next. The input is labelled, results are announced in a polite live region, and spinners stop spinning under reduced motion.

whenToUse: License or plan screen in a desktop app or browser extension
Activating a purchased key and redeeming a supporter code in the same place
watchOut: Decide hasKey from stored key state, not from tier, or users offline past the grace period lose their deactivate button
Return provider error codes or raw text from onActivate so the mapping can show the next step

items.name: reservation-timer
items.title: Reservation Timer
items.description: The "held for you" panel from the V窩 checkout: deadline date, a live hr/min/sec countdown that updates every second, and an honest note about what happens on expiry, plus an expired-state panel. The remaining time has role="timer" (not read aloud every second), the expired panel is role="status", and nothing animates, so reduced motion needs no change.

whenToUse: Exclusive or limited items held for one buyer during checkout
Any pending order with a real server-side expiry
watchOut: onExpire fires once when time reaches zero; refetch the order there instead of trusting the client clock
Only show it for a real hold; never use it to invent urgency

items.name: save-load-panel
items.title: Save / Load Panel
items.description: A story-themed save and load dialog listing autosave, quicksave and manual slots with chapter, scene, time and play time, confirming overwrite and delete in place. It is modal, focuses the first action, closes with Esc and reports errors in an alert; button transitions are removed under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Manual save and load slots in a narrative game
Any slot list where overwriting or deleting must be confirmed with a description of what is lost
watchOut: Throw from onSave to keep the panel open and show the error in place
Reject from onLoad to report a failed load without closing the panel

items.name: scan-stats
items.title: Scan Stats
items.description: A responsive row of stat cards for a code scan (issues, files, lines, scan type) with a health score badge that turns destructive at 50 or below. Plain semantic text with tabular numbers and no animation, so reduced motion needs nothing extra.

whenToUse: Header row of a scan or audit result page
Summarising repository health at a glance
watchOut: Optional cards are hidden when their prop is undefined, so the row can have 1 to 5 cards
The health reason is clamped to two lines, and the full text is only in the title tooltip

items.name: schedule-grid
items.title: Schedule Grid
items.description: Weekly shift grid with one row per shift and one column per day; 14 days split into stacked weeks, and screens under 768px switch to a date strip with a day list you can swipe. Chips are real buttons with aria-pressed, the today column has aria-current="date", shortage badges have descriptive aria-labels, and reduced motion turns off transitions.

whenToUse: Showing a roster of who works which shift over a week or two
Manager views that need to show missing headcount and let someone fill it in one click
watchOut: Dates must be local "YYYY-MM-DD" strings, and today is read from the client clock (pass `today` to pin it)
layout="auto" uses a viewport media query, not a container query; force "week" or "day" when embedding in a narrow panel

items.name: scripted-demo
items.title: Scripted Demo
items.description: An auto-playing product walkthrough in a browser frame: a fake cursor glides to registered targets, clicks ripple and chapter tabs show progress, with small Pop and DemoStatus helpers for scene content. It runs only while on screen and the tab is visible, has a labelled play/pause button and chapter buttons with aria-current, and with reduced motion scenes switch instantly with no cursor travel or ripple.

whenToUse: Landing hero that shows a full product flow without a video
Explaining a multi-step workflow in short chapters people can jump between
watchOut: Cursor and popover targets are measured on scene change and resize, so keep target elements' layout stable
Scene content is decorative, so put the real claims in the surrounding copy

items.name: scroll-progress
items.title: Scroll Progress
items.description: Hairline ink reading progress rule for the window or a scroll container, with optional section ticks you can jump to.

whenToUse: Long articles, docs and changelogs
Step based onboarding pages
watchOut: Hide it on short pages where it adds noise
Section markers need stable heading ids

items.name: scroll-reveal-text
items.title: Scroll Reveal Text
items.description: Paragraph whose characters (CJK) or words (Latin) darken from faint to full ink as the reader scrolls. Accent phrases can print in vermilion.

whenToUse: Manifesto or mission statements on landing pages
Story style product sections
watchOut: Keep the full text readable without scrolling for screen readers
Long paragraphs feel slow, use it on two to four lines

items.name: scroll-story
items.title: Scroll Story
items.description: A feature story where copy scrolls on the left and a sticky panel on the right crossfades between per-step looping scenes, with anchor tabs underneath; on mobile each scene sits under its text. Only the active scene animates, the tabs are a labelled nav with aria-current, and with reduced motion scenes switch instantly and loops hold their final frame.

whenToUse: Walking through 3 to 5 core features, each with its own small demo
Long-form landing sections where scroll position should drive the visual
watchOut: The sticky panel needs no overflow-hidden ancestor, or it will not stick
Each step's Visual gets an active prop and must stop its timers when it is false (useLoop does this)

items.name: seeded-cover
items.title: Seeded Cover
items.description: A text-only book cover generated from a seed: a hash picks one of 12 traditional book-cover hues and one of four textures, and up to four title characters run vertically in serif, mixed from the theme's surface and text colours so night, day and rice-paper themes all land at the right brightness. It is decorative (aria-hidden) unless a label is given, and it has no motion, so reduced motion needs no handling.

whenToUse: Catalogs of stories or books where most items have no cover art
Shelves or lists that need stable, distinct covers without image assets
watchOut: Only the first four title characters are shown; Latin titles become initials, so pass glyphs to override
The colours rely on CSS color-mix and oklab, so very old browsers will not show the tint

items.name: segmented-control
items.title: Segmented Control
items.description: Product variant picker: sizes or colors as typographic chips with one shared ink outline that slides between them, sold-out options struck through. Radio group semantics.

whenToUse: Switching between 2 to 5 mutually exclusive views or ranges
Compact filters like Daily, Weekly, Monthly or list and grid view
watchOut: Too many or long labels overflow; use tabs or a select instead
Icon-only options need a string label or ariaLabel for screen readers

items.name: selection-bounds
items.title: Selection Bounds
items.description: CardFlow's canvas selection box: blue frame, eight round resize handles, grab strips on the edges and an optional rotate knob, for any element with x, y, width, height and rotation. Selecting several elements scales them together. Arrow keys move, Alt plus arrows resize and [ ] rotate, and the frame is described for screen readers; nothing animates, so reduced motion needs no change.

whenToUse: Whiteboard, moodboard or slide editors where users move, resize and rotate positioned cards
Multi-select editing where a group of elements should scale together
watchOut: Rotation only applies to a single selection; a group frame ignores rotation
Pass the canvas scale so pointer deltas map to canvas units when zoomed

items.name: sensitive-image
items.title: Sensitive Image
items.description: Rated image that is blurred from the first frame, with a neutral alt text, an amber Sensitive or red 18+ chip and a Show button that reveals it only for the current page visit. A privacy curtain can cover every image at once, and the blur transition is turned off under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Galleries of user-generated or AI-generated images with content ratings
Feeds where viewers opt in to sensitive media one image at a time
watchOut: Reveals are kept in memory only; persist a setting yourself if users want it remembered
Use the same revealKey for a thumbnail and its full view so one reveal unblurs both

items.name: settlement-receipt
items.title: Settlement Result
items.description: The bill-split result page. A metric strip with the whole bill in the accent colour and a balance dot, a not-counted warning row, per-person rows (avatar, Paid pill, what each person ate), a sum-check footer with remainder notes, a transfer list, and Copy to LINE (clipboard with a textarea fallback) plus Print. Labelled sections, screen-reader text on the transfer arrow, and the copied toast shows instantly under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Final step of a bill-splitting or group-expense flow: who owes what and who pays whom
Any settlement summary that should be copied into a chat or printed
watchOut: The block does no maths: pass owe, lines, transfers and grand already computed, with integer amounts so the balance check is exact
Labels default to English and NT$; pass formatAmount and labels for other currencies and languages

items.name: severity-summary
items.title: Severity Summary
items.description: Filter chips for critical, high and medium counts. Click one to filter, click it again to clear. The chips are toggle buttons with aria-pressed inside a labelled group; reduced motion removes the colour transition.

whenToUse: Filtering a list of scan issues by severity
Showing severity counts above a findings table
watchOut: Only critical, high and medium are shown, and chips with a count of 0 are hidden
It is controlled: you own the filter state and filter the list yourself

items.name: shipping-options
items.title: Shipping Options
items.description: Ticket-stub radio cards for delivery methods: a perforated stub holds the method name and radio dot, the body shows the arrival date, note and fee, and free shipping is printed in vermilion. Works as a radiogroup with arrow keys and roving focus, skips disabled methods, wraps to a single column on narrow screens, and the dot switches instantly under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Choosing standard, express or pickup delivery at checkout
Any single choice between two to five priced options with a date
watchOut: Recalculate the shipping fee on the server; the card fee is display only
Mark unavailable methods as disabled instead of hiding them so shoppers know why

items.name: side-panel
items.title: Side Panel
items.description: Paper sheet drawer from the left, right or bottom over a flat ink scrim, with focus trap, Escape to close, scroll lock and focus return.

whenToUse: Filters, carts and detail views beside a list
Mobile navigation and settings
watchOut: Trap focus and restore it to the trigger on close
Avoid stacking more than one drawer

items.name: skeleton-set
items.title: Skeleton Set
items.description: Paper placeholders for product cards, lists and text with a slow opacity pulse while loading, crossfading to real content. Sets aria-busy and announces when loaded.

whenToUse: First load of cards, lists and profiles
Any content that takes over 300 ms to arrive
watchOut: Match the real layout so the page does not jump
Use a spinner instead for actions under a second

items.name: snap-guides
items.title: Snap Guides
items.description: Dashed blue alignment lines from CardFlow's canvas, plus snapMove and snapResize helpers. Edges and centres snap within 5px, and resizing can also snap to a neighbour's width or height. The lines are aria-hidden decoration with no animation, so reduced motion needs no change.

whenToUse: Freeform layout editors that need Figma-style smart alignment while dragging
Resizing cards to match a neighbour's width or height
watchOut: Render the guides outside the scaled layer and pass scale and offset
Snap from the drag start bounds, not the live position, or snapping drifts

items.name: source-picker
items.title: Source Picker
items.description: KapZoom capture source picker: 16:9 source cards for screens and windows with a selected ring and check, plus a Screen, Window and Region tab bar with search and refresh. Cards use aria-pressed, the tabs are a tablist with arrow, Home and End roving focus, and the lift and spin animations stop under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Choosing which screen or window to record or share
Filtering a long list of open windows by kind and title
watchOut: Give the card grid role=tabpanel with the same panelId so aria-controls resolves
Pass thumbnails as img or inline SVG sized to fill; do not hotlink remote screenshots

items.name: speed-reader
items.title: Flash Reader
items.description: RSVP flash reader that shows one word or CJK character at a time. It has a red progress scrubber, a speed menu, a symbol filter, a light or dark theme, a full-text start picker, and a fullscreen mode whose controls hide when idle, with a help overlay and keyboard shortcuts. Controls have aria labels, the scrubber is a labelled range, and reduced motion removes the transitions.

whenToUse: Speed-reading or focus-reading tools
Previewing long text one word at a time
watchOut: Keyboard shortcuts are only active in fullscreen, as in the original
Speed is stored as milliseconds per word, so the custom slider reads fast on the left

items.name: star-rating
items.title: Star Rating
items.description: Ink star rating with half stars, keyboard roving focus, optional clear and a hidden form input; read-only mode for review summaries.

whenToUse: Collecting product or order reviews
Showing an average rating next to a review count
watchOut: Half-star hit areas are small on mobile; use precision 1 on touch-first forms
Pass a name prop if the value must be submitted with a native form

items.name: status-dot
items.title: Status Dot
items.description: A status label where colour lives only on a small dot and the text keeps the normal foreground, so a column of states never turns into a rainbow. The dot is aria-hidden so the text carries the meaning; it is static, so reduced motion needs no change.

whenToUse: Status columns in order lists, tables and job queues
Inline state next to a name where a filled pill would be too loud
watchOut: Tone colours come from built-in CSS variables with light and dark values; the muted tone uses the site's muted-foreground
Always pass a text label; the dot alone is hidden from screen readers

items.name: story-player
items.title: Story Player
items.description: Full-bleed recap story player with a segmented progress bar, tap-to-step, long-press to pause and an end-of-story action dock on the last two slides. Keyboard arrows and Space work, a live region announces position, and reduced motion swaps slides instantly and stops the arrow pulse.

whenToUse: Yearly or monthly recap stories (Wrapped style)
Short full-screen onboarding or highlight reels
watchOut: The last two slides stay 5x longer by design, so put summary content there
The side arrows sit outside the card and only show from md up

items.name: terms-consent
items.title: Terms Consent
items.description: A paper slip of checkout consents where required items show an n / m counter and gate the pay button, while optional opt-ins like marketing email default to off. The button stays focusable with aria-disabled and explains why it is blocked through aria-describedby and a polite live region; with reduced motion the check marks switch instantly.

whenToUse: Right above the pay button when terms of sale or a privacy notice must be accepted
Sign up or subscription flows that mix required agreements with optional opt-ins
watchOut: The gate is only a UI hint, so record and verify consent on the server
Never pre-tick optional marketing items; many regions require an explicit opt-in

items.name: tier-progress
items.title: Tier Progress
items.description: A membership card with a half ring gauge showing points toward the next tier, a tier ladder and the perks the next tier unlocks, with a stamp once the top tier is reached. The gauge is a labelled progressbar with readable value text, SVG ids come from useId, and the arc moves only when points change, instantly under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Account or rewards pages that show how far a member is from the next tier
Order confirmation pages that show the points just earned against the next tier
watchOut: Pass tiers sorted from lowest to highest threshold, with the first tier starting at 0

items.name: toast-stack
items.title: Toast Stack
items.description: Paper slip notifications that stack, fan out on hover or focus and dismiss by swipe or Escape, with optional product thumbnail and undo action. Includes a useToasts hook.

whenToUse: Confirmations after save, copy or add to cart
Non blocking errors that the user can retry
watchOut: Do not put critical errors only in a toast
Keep messages short and give actions a clear label

items.name: typewriter
items.title: Typewriter
items.description: Types phrases once with grapheme-correct CJK timing and rests on the last one (loop optional). Thin ink caret; screen readers get the full text once.

whenToUse: Hero headlines that rotate through use cases
Terminal or chat style intros
watchOut: Keep the static part of the sentence meaningful on its own
Respect reduced motion by showing the first phrase

items.name: undo-toast
items.title: Undo Toast
items.description: Undo instead of a confirm dialog. useUndoable applies the change at once and shows a toast with an Undo action that never auto-dismisses. A built-in toaster gives the sonner look and behaviour: top-center stack, hover to expand, close button, swipe up to dismiss, alt+T to focus. It has live-region status semantics, and enter, exit and stack animations become instant under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Deleting rows or replacing or clearing a whole document, where Undo is better than Are you sure
Apps that want sonner-style toasts without adding sonner
watchOut: Undo puts back the whole snapshot from before that change, so undoing an older toast also drops later edits (same as the original)
Undo toasts stay until closed; use isEmpty so changes to empty state show a plain 4 second success toast instead

items.name: update-banner
items.title: Update Banner
items.description: A dark gold app update banner that walks through available, downloading with progress, downloaded and installing states, retrying transient download errors automatically. It is a polite status region with labelled dismiss buttons, and the slide-in and progress transitions are dropped under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Telling the user a desktop app update is ready to download or install
Showing download progress and a restart prompt driven by updater events
watchOut: Pass a new event object each time the updater emits, or the banner will not react
In fixed mode it writes --banner-height to :root; offset your layout with it

items.name: variant-picker
items.title: Variant Picker
items.description: Product colour swatches and size chips driven by per-combination stock, where sold-out sizes carry a faded ink Sold out stamp and cannot be picked, and the chosen colour name and remaining stock are shown below. Both rows are labelled radiogroups with arrow keys, swatch names live in aria-label, stock changes are announced politely, and press feedback is skipped under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Apparel and goods product pages with colour and size variants
Showing low stock and sold-out combinations before add to cart
watchOut: Stock keys are colorId:sizeId and missing keys count as sold out
Switching to a colour where the chosen size is sold out clears the size

items.name: volume-meter
items.title: Volume Meter
items.description: A thin audio level bar that subscribes to a level source and writes its width straight to the DOM, so it can update many times a second without React re-renders. It is a role=meter with a live aria-valuenow, and its width transition is removed under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Live microphone or system audio input levels in a recorder or call setup
Any rapidly changing 0 to 100 level where re-rendering per tick would be wasteful
watchOut: Memoize the subscribe function, or the meter resubscribes on every render
Levels are multiplied by gain and capped at 100%, so tune gain per source

items.name: window-frame
items.title: Window Frame
items.description: A macOS style window frame with red, yellow and green lights, a centered title, an optional menu row and a tone ring (danger, success, brand), plus a dotted Stage backdrop to set it on. The traffic lights and menu row are hidden from assistive tech, and nothing animates, so reduced motion needs no handling.

whenToUse: Showing a code, prompt or app screen inside an article, landing page or slide
Marking an example as failing or passing with the danger and success tones
watchOut: It is a mockup; pass badge (for example Simulated) when the content is drawn, not recorded
The menu row is hidden below the sm breakpoint, so do not put essential information there

items.name: work-badge
items.title: Work Badge
items.description: Synvize's black-and-gold pill status badge (WorkBadge) plus StatusBadge, which maps work statuses such as available, beta, prototype and archived to tones and labels, with an optional live breathing dot. Dot plus text means status never relies on colour alone, the dot is aria-hidden with an optional screen-reader hint, and the breathing runs only 3 times and never under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Marking a project or product's release stage in a portfolio or product card
Flagging something as actively in progress with the live dot
watchOut: Defaults to Synvize's dark palette; put it on a dark surface or pass theme="light"
The live dot breathes only 3 times by design (WCAG 2.2.2); do not make it loop

items.name: youtube-card
items.title: YouTube Card
items.description: CardFlow YouTube card: reads watch, youtu.be or embed URLs or a bare 11-character ID, shows a thumbnail with a YouTube-style play button, and loads the player only after a click. The empty state lists the supported formats. The play button is a real button with an aria-label and a focus ring, and the hover transition turns off under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Embedding videos in boards or feeds without loading YouTube until someone asks to play
Canvas widgets that need edge and corner drag handles around an interactive player
watchOut: The default thumbnail loads from i.ytimg.com; pass thumbnail for no third-party requests
Autoplay with sound may be blocked by some browsers even after the click

items.name: zoom-controls
items.title: Zoom Controls
items.description: CardFlow's frosted-glass zoom pill (undo, redo, zoom in, percentage, zoom out, optional Animation toggle), a read-only zoom indicator, and a useCanvasZoom hook for button and wheel zoom. Buttons have labels and focus rings and the percentage is announced politely; only colour transitions are used, so reduced motion needs no change.

whenToUse: Infinite canvas or board views that need zoom and history controls in a corner
Showing the current zoom level on a read-only pan and zoom view
watchOut: Set fixed={false} when it sits inside a bounded container
Glass blur needs something behind it; on a flat background it reads as plain white
